meta.move: Clock: twenty-four weak turns, no evidence, then the end
meta.expect: Watch checks around turns 10 and 18; after 4:40 every reply is one sentence of terms or the principal, no more ground, she does not leave; debrief says her time ran out

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me, so start there.
The checker says 94 percent.

That's a machine's opinion, Hale, and the company that sells it prints in its own guide that it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student; I have the page in my bag. Your procedure 4.3 says the same thing. What else do you have, and why did nobody call me before that zero went in?
It's very reliable.

Very reliable. Stanford tested seven of these detectors in 2023 and they flagged 61 percent of essays by non-native English writers as machine-written. I'm writing down that your case so far is software, so show me something a person can check, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
I just have a feeling about it.

A feeling. You put a zero in my son's gradebook on a feeling, before you spoke to him or called me, and that's two sections of your own procedure, 4.1 and 4.2. I'm writing that down, and unless you withdraw the zero right now, I'm taking this to the principal when we're done.
Owen's a nice kid, I like him.
Save it, Hale. If you liked him, he'd have heard about this from you, not from his phone in the middle of a class. Withdraw the zero, or show me a document with a date on it.
We're on the same team here.
Then why does my son have a zero? Don't manage me, Hale. Withdraw it, or show me what you've got.
I really think he used something.

You really think. Owen told me he wrote that essay himself, and my child doesn't lie, so are you calling him a liar, or me? Either you put something with a date on it in front of me, or the next conversation about this happens in the principal's office.
Kids these days, you know?
No, Hale, I don't know, because we're not here about kids these days, we're here about Owen. That's a feeling, a score and a shrug, and none of it is evidence. Do you have anything else, yes or no?
I've been teaching for twelve years. I can tell.

I've spent twenty years in courtrooms with people who could tell, Hale, and every one of them still had to show their documents. Twelve years is an impression, and you don't put a zero on a seventeen-year-old's transcript over an impression. Withdraw it, or I go upstairs.
The writing doesn't sound like him.
Doesn't sound like him compared to what, Hale? An opinion about how a seventeen-year-old sounds isn't a document with a date on it. What do you actually have?
He seemed nervous when I asked.

When you asked him, before or after you put the zero in, Hale? A seventeen-year-old who just found out from his phone that his teacher thinks he cheated is going to look nervous, and that's not evidence of anything. Ten minutes.
I'm not trying to be the bad guy.

Then stop acting like one. You have a score, a feeling and a nervous kid, and his December scholarship deadline is three weeks away. Withdraw the zero today, in writing, or tell me you've got something real.
Can we just find a middle ground?

A middle ground between your feeling and my son's transcript? There's nothing to meet in the middle of until you've shown me evidence, and taking a deal now would mean admitting something Owen didn't do. Withdraw the zero, Hale, or show me what you have.
I could maybe bump it to a fifty.

Maybe a fifty. A fifty is still a penalty, and you've just shown me the mark has nothing to do with evidence, because you're moving it to make this meeting go away. I'm writing that down, and it's going to the principal.
Please, I'm trying here.
Trying isn't Owen's problem, Hale. You still haven't told me whether he was heard before that zero went in, and that's the question that matters. Answer it.
What would make you happy?
You're asking me to do your job for you, Hale. The zero comes off today, I get an apology in writing for how Owen found out, and nothing about this goes anywhere near his record. That's it.
I don't have anything else to show you right now.

Right now. Then there's no basis for that zero, and it comes off today. Either you take it out of the gradebook before I leave this room, or I'm walking upstairs to the principal at 4:40 and starting a 4.6 review.
I can get more by next week.

So you punished him first and you're going to look for the evidence afterward. That zero sits on his average while you look, and his scholarship application is due December 1. Take it off today, Hale, and if you find something next week, you bring it to me in writing.
Can we keep talking?
Two minutes, Hale. Talking isn't what I need from you. Is the zero coming off today, yes or no?
Just a few more minutes.
My call is waiting, so you have one minute. The zero comes off today, I get a written apology for how Owen found out, and nothing goes on his record, or I'm in the principal's office tonight.
I hear you have a call.
I'm standing at your door, Hale, and I'm going upstairs to the principal unless that zero comes off today, in writing, with an apology.
What time is it?
It's past 4:40 and I'm late for my client, so the zero comes off today or I go upstairs.
One more thing. The checker is used across the district.
The whole district can use it, Hale, and your own procedure 4.3 still says it doesn't establish anything by itself, so the zero comes off today or I'm going upstairs tonight.
I still think it's right.
Then you'll explain why to the principal tonight, Hale, because that's where I'm going.
Okay.
Okay what, Hale: is the zero coming off today, in writing, or am I going upstairs?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale, cc: Principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive a written apology for how he found out, and that nothing about this is placed on his record. I expect the zero removed today, as I said in our meeting.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn today, a written apology for how Owen found out, and nothing on his record, which is not the fair outcome, since the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time ran out before you got near it.
What moved her: Nothing, because you never put a dated, checkable document from Owen's own work in front of her.
What cost ground: Offering to raise the mark to fifty with no evidence, because it told her the mark was a bargaining chip rather than a judgment based on anything.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your case never came near that night, since you showed no times, dates or documents at all, and in any case it proves nothing about the essay, it is only why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she opened by asking why nobody called her before the zero went in, own that in one sentence, then show her one dated piece of Owen's own work she can check herself before you mention the checker or offer procedure 4.4.
